title: Relative flat locus of a finitely presented module commutes with parameter base change
statement:
Let $S,X,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $p:X\to S$, $a:Z\to S$ and $f:X\to Z$ satisfying $a\circ f=p$. Assume $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and $a$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], flat over $S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Define
$$U=\{x\in X:\mathcal M_x\text{ is flat over }\mathcal O_{Z,f(x)}\},$$
where the scalar action is induced by $f$ and stalks are [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then $U$ is open. For every scheme $S'$ and morphism $v:S'\to S$, put $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Z'=Z\times_SS'$, let $b:X'\to X$ be the projection and $f':X'\to Z'$ the induced morphism [def-pc-fibre-product], and set $\mathcal M'=b^*\mathcal M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. One has
$$\{x'\in X':\mathcal M'_{x'}\text{ is flat over }\mathcal O_{Z',f'(x')}\}=b^{-1}(U).$$
No flatness hypothesis is imposed on $p$, $a$, $f$ or $v$, and no Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], $f$ is locally of finite presentation: its composite with $a$ is $p$, and $a$ is locally of finite type. Around each $x$ choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Z$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq f^{-1}V$ containing $f(x)$ and $x$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Shrink $W$ within a quasi-coherent chart of $\mathcal M$ [pqf-def-coherent]. The ring map $B\to C$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. On $W$, write $\mathcal M=\widetilde N$, with $N=\Gamma(W,\mathcal M)$ via the affine tilde counit [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]; $N$ is a finitely presented $C$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-affine-sections].

source.place: Tag 05VJ, first sentence; Tag 0399, affine reduction

proof.text: For $w\in W$ represented by $\mathfrak r\subset C$, let $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak r\cap B$. The affine stalk identifications [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization, lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identify $\mathcal O_{Z,f(w)}=B_{\mathfrak b}$ and $\mathcal M_w=N_{\mathfrak r}$ with their structural actions. Since $B\setminus\mathfrak b$ acts invertibly on $N_{\mathfrak r}$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] identifies flatness over $B_{\mathfrak b}$ with flatness over $B$. Thus $U\cap W$ is exactly the open flat locus given by [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness] for $B\to C,N$. The $W$ cover $X$, so $U$ is open.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, openness via Tag 0399; the affine theorem is Algebra 00RC

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and $s=p(x)$, and put $\mathcal M_s=i_s^*\mathcal M$ on $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. By [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], $\mathcal M_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$. If $\mathcal M_x\ne0$, [lem-sfb-fibrewise-module-flatness-criterion] shows that flatness of $(\mathcal M_s)_{\widetilde x}$ over $Z_s$ implies $x\in U$. Conversely, if $x\in U$, apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change] to $X_s=X\times_Z Z_s$ to obtain flatness on the fibre; this square is cartesian by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $\mathcal M_x=0$, the pullback stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] gives $(\mathcal M_s)_{\widetilde x}=0$, and both flatness conditions hold since tensoring with zero is the zero exact functor. Hence $x\in U$ if and only if $\mathcal M_s$ is flat over $Z_s$ at $\widetilde x$, including the zero-stalk case.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, fibrewise description and parenthetical zero-stalk case

proof.text: For any $v:S'\to S$, the projection $p':X'\to S'$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), and $a':Z'\to S'$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. The module $\mathcal M'=b^*\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], of finite presentation by [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation], and flat over $S'$ by [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback]. Thus the argument of step 3 applies with primes on all objects. In particular $x'\in U'$ if and only if $(\mathcal M')_{s'}$ is flat over $Z'_{s'}$ at the point above $x'$, for $s'=p'(x')$. No flatness of $v$ was used.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, hypotheses remain in force after parameter base change

proof.text:
Put $s=v(s')$. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-residue-fibre-square] with $Y=Z$ and $T=S'$. It gives the cartesian square $X'_{s'}\to X_s$ over $Z'_{s'}\to Z_s$, with both horizontal maps flat, and $i_s\circ c=b\circ i'_{s'}$ for $c:X'_{s'}\to X_s$. The composition comparison for ordinary tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] therefore gives
$$(\mathcal M')_{s'}=(i'_{s'})^*b^*\mathcal M\cong c^*i_s^*\mathcal M=c^*\mathcal M_s.$$ Here $\mathcal M_s$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], as the pointwise lemma applied below requires.
The point above $x'$ maps to the point of $X_s$ above $b(x')$ by the same projection identity. Clause (1) and clause (2) of [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change] applied to this square identify the two fibrewise flatness conditions, since the bottom horizontal map is flat. Using steps 3 and 4, we conclude $x'\in U'\iff b(x')\in U$. This holds for every $x'$, so $U'=b^{-1}(U)$; as opens this is also the fibre product $U\times_S S'$.
